name: Matches, by season, model or owner
description: One statement, three listings: a season's matches, one version's history (?model=), or every match a person's versions played (?owner=). Each row carries ALL of its seats, because the seats block is one component. TRIALS ARE PRIVATE -- a trial seats a candidate nobody else may see yet -- so the season listing excludes them and only a query naming the model returns them; the queued, cancelled and failed rows only an owner may see are GET /v1/me/matches, a route of its own rather than a parameter here. Pagination is a KEYSET on (played_at, id): played_at is written once and never moves, so a position here cannot drift the way a live ladder's does. `total` is the filtered count, returned on the first page only, because it is the one part that must scan. `players_min` and `players_max` bound the SEAT COUNT, inclusive, so the site's 2 / 3-4 / 5-8 tabs are two numbers and not a list of boards: how many play is the map's, not the game's. `?map=` is a board's id within the season, and `season` is its slug.
